supersedes: the 2026-08-30 estimate of 5.5 x 3.75 x 3.5 m, which was 24 cm out on ceiling height and ~45 cm out on wall length
units_note: Source values are centimetres, recorded here in metres. The note gives each wall as height x length.
ceiling_note: Mean of the four wall heights. The room's own ceiling varies by 0.5 cm corner to corner, which is a third of the 1.5 cm gate and is a floor on achievable accuracy: our pipeline cannot be more consistent than the ceiling is flat. This belongs in the error budget.
shape_note: Opposite walls A and C differ by 8.0 cm (1.6%); B and D agree exactly. The room is genuinely not square, which is why per-wall ground truth was needed and why the earlier length-and-breadth version could not have scored a gate.

CONFLICT.what: Floor long dimension is written 457.7 cm, but wall C measures 497.7 cm and wall A 505.7 cm.
CONFLICT.size: 40 cm against wall C — 8% of the wall length, which is the entire photo-tier gate.

readings.if_457_7_is_correct: The clear floor is shorter than the wall, so something occupies 40 cm along that run — a wardrobe, alcove, chimney breast or built-in. Then floor area is 15.24 m2 and the pipeline should recover the wall, not the clear floor.
readings.if_it_is_a_slip_for_497_7: Floor is 3.33 x 4.977 m, area 16.57 m2, fully consistent with wall C.

CONFLICT.resolution: unresolved — must not be guessed, it is gate-sized

openings.note: Door height 1.85 m is low against a 2.0-2.1 m modern standard, but consistent with older construction and with the 3.26 m ceiling.

open_questions: Resolve the 40 cm floor-versus-wall conflict above.
Which wall carries the door, and which carries the window? Opening detection is scored per surface, so an opening on the wrong wall scores as one miss plus one phantom.
Tape or laser? The brief asks for one of the two and the answer sets the ground-truth uncertainty we are entitled to quote.
Wall ordering: is A-B-C-D clockwise or anticlockwise, and which is the entry wall? Needed to align our output to this key.
